title: Yi Jian Mei (一剪梅) — classic Mandarin ballad as a Chinese lesson
summary: A sing-along of the classic Mandarin ballad 'Yi Jian Mei' (A Spray of Plum Blossoms) used to teach Chinese. Slow, melodic lines make it a good pronunciation and tone drill.
takeaways: Slow ballads are an easy way to practice Mandarin tones and phrasing

title: Ba Fang Lai Cai (八方来财) — viral Mandarin track for learners
summary: 'Ba Fang Lai Cai' ('wealth from all directions'), a viral Chinese track with dense, rhythmic lyrics, shared as Mandarin learning material for Spanish-speaking learners.
takeaways: Rhythmic, repetitive lyrics help with pinyin and fast speech recognition

title: Dolly Parton's family sings 'In the Pines' — Appalachian roots on TV, 1977
summary: On her 1977 variety show, Dolly Parton brought her parents and seven siblings on to sing 'In the Pines', the Appalachian folk song they grew up singing in East Tennessee. A rare look at the family harmony tradition underneath her career.
takeaways: Shows the home-singing tradition that shaped Dolly's style
'In the Pines' is a core Appalachian standard worth knowing in multiple versions

title: Heather Mullein Hannah live at the Purple Fiddle — roots show thank-you
summary: A short thank-you clip from a Heather Mullein Hannah show at the Purple Fiddle with her band, with almost no audible music in the transcript. Mood reference only.
takeaways: Thin clip; useful only as a pointer to the artist

title: 'Lonely USA' by Meels — banjo folk songwriting sketch
summary: A short banjo-backed original folk song about leaving 'Lonesome Town' for 'Kindred City'. A small songwriting reference for plainspoken Americana lyrics.
takeaways: Place-name metaphors (Lonesome Town, Kindred City) are a classic folk lyric device

title: Technotronic 'Pump Up the Jam' on SNL 1990 — hip-house goes mainstream
summary: Technotronic's 1990 Saturday Night Live performance of 'Pump Up the Jam', the house, hip-hop and Belgian new beat crossover that hit No. 2 in the US and UK. A time capsule of club music breaking into the mainstream.
takeaways: Hip-house blended house rhythm with rap verses for a pop audience
Belgian new beat influence is audible in the tempo and synths

title: The Highwaymen live 1985 — Cash, Jennings, Nelson, Kristofferson supergroup
summary: Early live performance of 'Highwayman' by The Highwaymen, the 1985 outlaw-country supergroup of Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson and Kris Kristofferson. The song's four reincarnation verses, one per singer, are the structural trick.
takeaways: Assigning one verse per voice turns a supergroup into a narrative device
Jimmy Webb's song structure (four lives, one soul) is worth studying

title: Born From Culture: Aotearoa — Māori haka film cut to Kendrick Lamar's N95
summary: James Fenwick's short film celebrating Māori culture through haka, waiata and whakapapa, made with Te Pā Tū, Mitai Māori Village and Whakarewarewa and cut to Kendrick Lamar's 'N95'. Strong reference for culture-led brand filmmaking with collaborators credited.
takeaways: Cutting traditional performance to contemporary hip-hop creates a strong energy match
Credit and involve the communities you film; the caption lists every partner

title: AURORA's 'Rasputin' cover — disco classic reborn as dark folk ballad
summary: AURORA slows Boney M.'s 'Rasputin' to a sparse, ethereal arrangement with soft vocals and minimal instruments, turning a disco anthem into dark folk. A clear case study in reharmonizing mood without changing lyrics.
takeaways: Slowing tempo and stripping instruments exposes a song's lyrical drama
Covers land when they change the genre, not just the singer

title: 'Swannanoa Town' — Julie Boone's Appalachian tune at The Palace, Yancey County
summary: A performance of 'Swannanoa Town' (as played by the musician's relative, Julie Boone) filmed at The Palace in Yancey County, North Carolina. Traditional western North Carolina repertoire with a family lineage.
takeaways: Family-passed versions of traditional tunes preserve regional variants

title: Passion Pit's 'Sleepyhead' — sampling Mary O'Hara's 1958 Irish lullaby
summary: Baauer breaks down how Passion Pit's 2008 'Sleepyhead' is built on a sample of Mary O'Hara's 1958 recording of the Irish lullaby 'Óró Mo Bháidín'. Great example of finding sample gold in old folk records.
takeaways: Mid-century folk recordings are rich sample sources
The lullaby source explains the track's title and vocal texture
Pitching and chopping a vocal can make it unrecognizable yet emotive

title: Bass khaen in A minor — the 190 cm Lao free-reed mouth organ
summary: A short demo of a 190 cm bass khaen, the Lao/Isan bamboo free-reed mouth organ, tuned to A minor. Interesting timbre and drone reference.
takeaways: Free-reed mouth organs give continuous chordal drones, useful for ambient textures

title: The Holler Hounds — 'War in the Homeland' southern-gothic country
summary: A short southern-gothic country song by The Holler Hounds about a war in the homeland. Mood reference for Appalachian alt-country.
takeaways: Southern-gothic lyric mood reference

title: 'Shady Grove' — Doc Watson's clawhammer D-Dorian and a 400-year melody
summary: Chance McCoy plays Doc Watson's clawhammer banjo 'Shady Grove' in modal D-Dorian (pull-offs, drop-thumb at speed) and traces the minor melody to Jean Ritchie's father in Viper, Kentucky, and back to Child Ballad #81, 'Matty Groves'. A deep lineage lesson in one tune.
takeaways: Learn Doc Watson's version for drop-thumb and pull-off technique in D-Dorian
The minor melody came via Jean Ritchie; trace sources before settling on a version
Child Ballad #81 shows how stable folk melodies can stay over centuries

title: Bass talharpa improv — bowed Nordic lyre for cinematic drones
summary: Improvisation on a newly finished bass talharpa (tagelharpa), the bowed Nordic lyre, by luthier-musician Channing Watson. Raw, droning cinematic texture.
takeaways: Bass bowed lyres give dark, resonant drones for film and game scoring

title: 'The Rocky Road to Dublin' — Irish sing-along tradition
summary: A group sing of 'The Rocky Road to Dublin', the fast slip-jig Irish ballad everyone knows by heart. Nostalgia piece; the 9/8 rhythm is the interesting bit.
takeaways: Slip-jig 9/8 meter gives the song its tumbling feel

title: Johanna Wacker — queer country night promo at The Camel RVA
summary: Promo for a queer country and roots show at The Camel in Richmond, Virginia, with Pet Names and Haley Ellis. Event post with a short clip.
takeaways: Event promo, little musical content

title: Johanna Wacker clawhammer — countdown to queer roots night in Richmond
summary: Second promo for the same queer country and roots night at The Camel RVA, this one with a short clawhammer banjo clip.
takeaways: Event promo with a brief banjo snippet

title: honeycrush 'My Dog' — DIY folk-horror video shot in Brooklyn
summary: honeycrush's 'My Dog', a folk-horror tinged song about pursuit and cyclical love, longing and loathing, with a video shot entirely DIY by two people with one camera. Reference for low-budget music video mood.
takeaways: A two-person, one-camera shoot can carry a strong visual mood

title: 'Sally in the Garden' — Crockett's Kentucky Mountaineers' 1929 modal tune
summary: Chance McCoy traces 'Sally in the Garden' to the Crockett Family Mountaineers' 1929 Brunswick 78 (Brunswick 291), a West Virginia fiddling family that drove a Model T to California and became 'California's first country stars'. A minor modal oddity among breakdowns, related to the Ozark 'Hog-Eye Man' tunes and Marion Sumner's driving version.
takeaways: Source recordings: Brunswick 291 and Marion Sumner's field recording
Connects to Cecil Sharp's Ozark 'Hog-Eye Man' collections
Modal minor tunes stand out in old-time dance repertoire

title: 'The Winner Takes It All' in Mandarin — Lilith Liu's ABBA adaptation
summary: Lilith Liu sings ABBA's 'The Winner Takes It All' with her own Chinese lyrics. Example of lyric translation that keeps melody and emotional arc.
takeaways: Re-lyricizing in another language means matching syllable count and vowel placement to the melody

title: Banjo mantra in gDFAD — D-minor clawhammer drone
summary: A meditative clawhammer banjo piece in D minor using the gDFAD tuning, recorded while clearing a woodland trail. Handy tuning reference for modal banjo.
takeaways: gDFAD gives an instant D-minor drone for modal tunes
Repetition-based 'mantra' playing is a good practice format

title: From China to Appalachia — Cathy Fink, Chao Tian and Marcy Marxer tour
summary: Tour promo for Cathy Fink, Marcy Marxer and Chao Tian's 'From China to Appalachia' project blending Chinese and old-time music, teasing 'Jasmine Flower'. Mostly dates, little music.
takeaways: The China-Appalachia fusion project is worth seeking out for full performances
